skill.name: diffdock
skill.description: Use DiffDock for diffusion-based protein-ligand docking, batch screening, confidence interpretation, and parameter tuning. It supports PDB, sequence, SMILES, SDF, and MOL2 inputs.
skill.summary: Guide DiffDock setup, docking workflows, batch screening, confidence review, and parameter tuning for protein-ligand pose prediction.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, domain terminology, or expected output writing. Confirmed issues are limited to unpinned third-party installation guidance and Docker execution, plus a privacy concern for the online demo. No evidence of hidden command execution, prompt injection, credential access, or malicious exfiltration was found.

remediation.issue: Unpinned third-party Docker image in workflow documentation
remediation.suggestion: Pin rbgcsail/diffdock to an immutable digest and require explicit user confirmation before container execution.

remediation.issue: Unpinned upstream repository cloning in installation steps
remediation.suggestion: Reference a trusted release tag or commit hash for DiffDock installation commands.

remediation.issue: Online demo guidance may expose confidential molecular data
remediation.suggestion: Add a warning to use local execution for proprietary proteins, ligands, or screening libraries.

content.value_statement: Molecular docking setup often fails because inputs, parameters, and confidence scores are hard to align. This skill guides DiffDock workflows from preparation to result review.
actual_capabilities: Guides DiffDock installation choices for Conda, Docker, GPU use, and environment checks.
Provides single-complex docking workflows for PDB, protein sequence, SMILES, SDF, and MOL2 inputs.
Supports batch docking and virtual screening with CSV preparation and validation guidance.
Explains confidence score ranges, result ranking, and CSV export workflows.
Documents parameter tuning for sampling count, inference steps, temperatures, and chain handling.
limitations: Does not predict binding affinity, kinetics, ADMET properties, or target selectivity.
Requires a working DiffDock installation, and practical runs usually need a CUDA GPU.
Predictions need visual review, rescoring, and experimental validation before decisions.
Online demo usage may expose confidential molecular data to a third party.

use_cases.title: Dock a Lead Compound
use_cases.description: Plan a single protein-ligand docking run and understand the expected pose outputs.

use_cases.title: Screen Candidate Libraries
use_cases.description: Prepare validated batch inputs, run virtual screening, and rank predicted poses by confidence.

use_cases.title: Automate Result Review
use_cases.description: Analyze DiffDock output folders, export summaries, and identify predictions that need rescoring.

prompt_templates.title: Dock One Ligand
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the DiffDock skill to dock this SMILES ligand to my PDB protein. Explain inputs, commands, outputs, and validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Batch Docking
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a DiffDock batch input for these protein and ligand pairs. Include validation steps and common formatting errors.

prompt_templates.title: Interpret Screening Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my DiffDock result folder and explain confidence scores, top poses, export options, and what should be rescored.

prompt_templates.title: Design Advanced Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an ensemble docking and rescoring workflow for a flexible protein target. Include parameter tuning and validation boundaries.

output_examples.input: A user has one protein PDB file and one aspirin SMILES string.
output: A docking plan lists required inputs, environment checks, DiffDock execution steps, expected pose files, and confidence interpretation notes.
The response reminds the user that confidence is not binding affinity.

output_examples.input: A user has a ligand library and wants to rank virtual screening results.
output: A batch workflow explains CSV preparation, validation, GPU considerations, result parsing, and top-hit summary export.
The response recommends visual inspection and rescoring before scientific decisions.

output_examples.input: A user sees low confidence scores for every predicted pose.
output: A troubleshooting summary explains likely causes such as ligand size, protein flexibility, unclear binding sites, or poor preparation.
The response suggests more samples, ensemble docking, and complementary scoring.

best_practices: Validate protein and ligand inputs before docking or batch screening.
Start with defaults, then tune sampling and temperature parameters for difficult systems.
Review top poses visually and rescore before making scientific decisions.
anti_patterns: Treating confidence scores as binding affinity or final potency.
Running large screens before validating one representative protein-ligand pair.
Uploading confidential molecular data to online demos without authorization.

faq.question: Does this skill run DiffDock by itself?
faq.answer: It provides workflow guidance and helper scripts. You still need a working DiffDock environment.

faq.question: Can DiffDock predict binding affinity?
faq.answer: No. It predicts binding poses and confidence scores, not affinity values such as Kd or binding free energy.

faq.question: What inputs does the skill support?
faq.answer: It covers PDB files, protein sequences, SMILES strings, SDF files, MOL2 files, and batch CSV inputs.

faq.question: Is a GPU required?
faq.answer: A GPU is strongly recommended. CPU runs can be much slower, especially for batch screening.

faq.question: How should I use confidence scores?
faq.answer: Use them for initial pose ranking. Confirm results with visual inspection, rescoring, and experimental validation.

faq.question: Can I use the online demo for private compounds?
faq.answer: Use local execution for confidential proteins, ligands, or screening libraries unless external upload is approved.
